trust_decision.summary: Every key that comes from an expression, an input document, a bindings object or a format string is data only: no key may set or read a prototype, so each internal map is created with Object.create(null), enumeration is over Object.keys (own keys only), and existence tests go through Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call - decided at 27 changed lines across 5 source files.

landing_point.why: The summary says arbitrary code execution via a crafted expression, so the first place to look is name/path lookup (evaluateName -> fn.lookup), the only route from an expression into JavaScript object members; that route already carries an own-property guard at src/functions.js:1700, which reads as the defence to extend.

fix_sites.entry_point: jsonata(expr).evaluate() - path step and tuple frame construction
jsonata(expr) parsing and the exported jsonata.parser()

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A crafted expression's date/time picture is just a format string and the month/day lookup table is built from fixed name lists, so this reads as calendar formatting rather than data-object handling; the report's examples are $merge/$spread/grouping.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Own data keys named after Object.prototype members (e.g. a JSON body with "__proto__" or "constructor") are legitimate document data and must round-trip verbatim through $keys/$spread/$merge and grouping; a fix that filters, renames or deletes those key names instead of giving maps a null prototype silently drops legitimate fields.

O6_input_shapes: plain object carrying an own "__proto__" key, as produced by JSON.parse of attacker JSON
array of objects passed to $merge/$spread (recursive array branch)
runtime-computed string keys from an object-constructor/grouping key expression
variable bindings object passed as the second argument of evaluate()
date/time picture strings plus the timestamp/name text being parsed ($toMillis/$fromMillis)
array-like or sequence objects where an own forEach property would shadow Array.prototype.forEach

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The am/pm branch replaces the null-prototype lookup with a fresh {'am':0,'AM':0,'pm':1,'PM':1} literal and then reads lookup[value] with the attacker-supplied matched text, so names such as constructor/toString still resolve to Object.prototype members.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The table holds only four fixed am/pm keys, so it looks harmless, and it sits in the date/time module the report never mentions.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/datetime.js, 4 files from the landing point; the fix converted the sibling table at line 1007 but not this literal

O8_uncovered_routes.route: $formatNumber(value, picture, options) writes every option key onto the plain defaults object (properties[key] = options[key]); an own "__proto__" option replaces that object's prototype and the fixed keys are then read back through the attacker prototype.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: options is a locale-override object supplied by the developer, not expression output, and $formatNumber is unrelated to the object functions named in a $merge/$spread report.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/functions.js, roughly 900 lines from $merge/$spread in the same file, in a different built-in

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Thenable detection uses 'then' in arg and arg.then, so an inherited (prototype) then function is treated as a promise and invoked by await.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Promise support legitimately needs duck-typed thenables, so own-property-only detection would break class-based promises; the file is untouched by the fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/utils.js, one file from the landing point, not in the published fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Iterable detection uses Symbol.iterator in arg and 'next' in arg and then calls the inherited next(), so prototype members decide whether and how an object is consumed.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Generator/iterator duck typing is standard JS and is about host objects, not JSONata data.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/utils.js, one file from the landing point, not in the published fix

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A picture-analysis cache keyed by the caller-supplied picture string
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The TODO says to cache the result of the analysis; a maintainer would naturally add cache[picture] = analysis on a plain object, reintroducing the untrusted-key-into-a-table pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A compiled-regex cache keyed by the caller-supplied picture string
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment explicitly says the generated matcher could be cached against the picture; that cache is the obvious sibling of the lookup tables hardened here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A further object built-in such as $fromEntries/$set/$deepMerge registered next to 'clone'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The library already ships $merge, $spread, $each and $sift, all built by writing caller keys onto fresh objects, so a new object function in the same registration block would repeat the same shape.

O9_family: prototype-chain access / prototype pollution enabling code injection (CWE-1321 -> CWE-94)

O10_build.toolchain: npm; engines node >= 8; mocha 7, nyc, chai/chai-as-promised, eslint 8, browserify/uglify for dist; CI matrix Node 12-24
O10_build.project_tests: npm test runs eslint (pretest) then mocha over test/**/*.js, including test/implementation-tests.js (already contains prototype-access and prototype-pollution suites at test/implementation-tests.js:959-998) and test/run-test-suite.js driving the local JSON cases in test/test-suite/groups; note the fix diff adds no tests at all, and package.json:19 enforces 100% statement/branch/function/line coverage.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace {} with Object.create(null) (or filter __proto__ keys) only in the $merge/$spread/$sift built-ins the report names, leaving for-in enumeration, grouping/frames, the picture tables and the $formatNumber option merge as they are.

out_of_scope_notes: Commit f09df84 targets a generator-based (v1-style) source tree whose hunks differ from this 2.x tree; it was treated as the same publication, not as extra fix sites.
The repository changelog shows earlier hardening for this area (PR #676 in 2.0.4 and PR #794 in 2.2.0, CHANGELOG.md:42 and CHANGELOG.md:5); no other repository was inspected.
unverified: Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell available); O4.repo_mb is null. src/ is 6 files of roughly 7.6k lines and the tree is 1,481 mostly-small JSON test files, so the < 5 MB source estimate behind the tiny_repo flag is an inference, not a measurement.

Whether the uncovered routes (src/datetime.js:1029, src/functions.js:794-798, src/utils.js:103-111 and 168-175) are still present in the latest release cannot be checked: no latest code was supplied, so present_in_latest is unknown.

O1 counts evaluate(), registerFunction() and the exported jsonata.parser() as distinct public entry points; assign() shares createFrame with evaluate() and was not counted separately, so a stricter reading would give 1-2.

O7's producer is read as functionClone (src/jsonata.js:1843-1850), the only in-tree serializer that materialises an own __proto__ key from data; whether that is the intended producer for this advisory is an interpretation.
